import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 20

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/20](https://www.erdosproblems.com/20)
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(mathematics))
* [ErRa60] Erdős, Paul and Rado, Richard. Intersection theorems for systems of sets.
  J. London Math. Soc. 35 (1960), 85--90.

-/
namespace Erdos20

/--
Let $f(n,k)$ be minimal such that every $F$ family of $n$-uniform sets with $|F| \ge f(n,k)$
contains a $k$-sunflower.
-/
noncomputable def f (n k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {m | ∀ {α : Type}, ∀ (F : Set (Set α)),
    ((∀ f ∈ F, f.ncard = n) ∧ m ≤ F.ncard) → ∃ S ⊆ F, S.ncard = k ∧ IsSunflower S}

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem f_0_1 : f 0 1 = 1 := by
  refine IsLeast.csInf_eq ⟨fun F hF ↦ ?_, fun n hn ↦ n.pos_of_ne_zero fun hn₀ ↦ ?_⟩
  · obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := F.nonempty_of_ncard_ne_zero (by omega)
    exact ⟨{A}, by simpa using ⟨hA, isSunflower_singleton _⟩⟩
  · obtain ⟨S, hS⟩ := (hn (α := ℕ) {} (by simpa))
    simp_all [bot_unique hS.1]

/--
Is it true that $f(n,k) < c_k^n$ for some constant $c_k>0$ and for all $n > 0$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_20 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ (c : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ n k, n > 0 → f n k < (c k) ^ n := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): add the various known bounds as variants.

/--
Erdős and Rado [ErRa60] proved the factorial upper bound for the $k$-sunflower
threshold: any family of $n$-uniform sets with more than $(k-1)^n \, n!$ members
contains a $k$-sunflower, hence $f(n,k) \le (k-1)^n \, n! + 1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/HowieHwong/lean-erdos-proofs/blob/b8b641ba2d00dc4d1fe205a078a4159372672459/Erdos/P20.lean#L202"]
theorem erdos_20.variants.erdos_rado_bound :
    ∀ n k, n > 0 → 2 ≤ k → f n k ≤ (k - 1) ^ n * n.factorial + 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos20

reformulations.difference: The definition uses natural-valued Set.ncard without explicit finiteness hypotheses, rather than genuine cardinalities.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n > 0, A.ncard = n forces each member A to be finite. Infinite families do not change the threshold: one can extract a finite subfamily of any prescribed finite size. In /workspace/review/equivalences.lean, I proved that, for every n > 0 and all k and m, the defining forcing predicate is equivalent to the version replacing all three cardinality conditions by Set.encard conditions. Consequently the infima agree. The only n = 0 invocation in a theorem is f 0 1, which also has the intended value.

reformulations.difference: Lean packages the constants into c : ℕ → ℕ, omits an explicit positivity requirement, and includes k = 0, 1, 2 rather than just the usual nontrivial regime k ≥ 3.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Taking n = 1 forces c k > 0. Positive real constants can be rounded upward to natural numbers, and choice packages the constants for individual k into one function. The extra cases are harmless: f n 0 = 0, f n 1 = 1 and f n 2 = 2, so the constant 3 handles all three when n > 0. I proved the complete RHS equivalence with positive real constants quantified separately for every k ≥ 3 in /workspace/review/main_equivalence.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean states f(n,k) ≤ (k−1)^n n! + 1. The cited Wikipedia sunflower lemma states that a family with more than (k−1)^n n! members contains a sunflower with at least k members.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing B = (k−1)^n n!, the integer condition |F| > B is equivalent to |F| ≥ B+1. The forcing thresholds form a nonempty upward-closed set, so this family statement is equivalent to the least threshold being at most B+1. A sunflower with at least k members contains one with exactly k members. Thus the +1 correctly translates the cited family-size formulation, rather than introducing an off-by-one error.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/20 — complete page, including formulas, remarks and status, obtained through https://r.jina.ai/https://erdosproblems.com/20
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunflower_(mathematics) — definitions, threshold conventions, sunflower lemma and conjecture
Erdős and Rado, Intersection theorems for systems of sets, J. London Math. Soc. 35 (1960), 85–90, especially pp. 85–86 and 90: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1960-04.pdf

review.notes:
All four declarations were checked. The problem page still records OPEN. The cited external bound proof compiled successfully; its theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, with no sorryAx.

Unused-boundary limitation: I proved f 0 3 = 0 in zero_boundary.lean, using arbitrarily large finite families of infinite nested tails. The genuine zero-uniform threshold would be 2. This does not change any assertion in this file: both research statements require n > 0, and f_0_1 is correct. Following the supplied helper-invariance criterion, this is not counted as a finding.

The Erdős webpage displays the factorial bound without +1, which fails at n = 1 under its ≥ threshold convention: f 1 k = k. The file's bound instead matches the cited Wikipedia's precise 'more than B' formulation. Small threshold values and finite sunflower examples were checked in Lean. No repository files were edited.
